Typical path: graduate from a secondary vocational school or associate program in rehabilitation therapy technology, nursing, or a related field -> start as a therapy aide -> learn assessment and training from therapists while working -> pursue rehabilitation therapist certification when possible -> advance into therapy or rehabilitation management.

Best suited to patient, energetic people who enjoy working with older adults and patients. If you can crouch to tie a patient's shoes and support them through one lap without resenting the pace, this work suits you.

Occupational therapy aides work under occupational therapists or occupational therapy assistants. They prepare and maintain treatment areas and equipment, assist patients with daily-activity training such as dressing, eating, and hand function, and handle records, cleaning, and other administrative work.

paragraphs: In the morning, prepare the day's equipment according to treatment orders, move wheelchairs into the training area, and wait for the first patient. During training, support the exercise ball, count several sets, and remind the patient to breathe. Help older adults with limited mobility onto and off the table and explain precautions to families. In the afternoon, disinfect equipment, enter records, and organize tools for tomorrow's schedule.

In one sentence: manage the treatment area and equipment and support patients safely. Duties include equipment preparation and disinfection, training assistance, observation and feedback, scheduling, and registration.

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show that about 5,200 occupational therapy aides were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 5,300 by 2034, a net increase of about 100 jobs, with roughly 600 openings per year and a median annual wage of about $37,400 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace occupational therapy aides, but it will take over scheduling, records, and equipment inventories. Hands-on transfers, training support, companionship, and observation of patient condition all require face-to-face human care.

If you want a rehabilitation career, do not stop at aide. Study rehabilitation therapy technology or nursing and build foundations in anatomy, assessment, and therapeutic techniques. Learn rehabilitation-assistance equipment in the AI era and aim for therapist certification.

Let software handle schedules and records, and use the saved time to learn therapists' techniques. Prioritize organizations that develop aides into therapists. Do not let aide remain your job label for ten years.

Do not hire aides based only on efficiency. Prioritize rehabilitation or nursing fundamentals and the ability to observe patients. Organizations that fund aide training and therapist certification retain people at clearly higher rates.
